name: Burgruine Ehrenberg
kurzbeschreibung: The Gothic core castle Ehrenberg from the 13th century features massive curtain walls, bastions, and vistas of highline179.
beschreibung:
Overview

The storied Burgruine Ehrenberg crowns a prominent forested hill at an altitude of 1,100 meters south of Reutte in the Tyrolean Außerfern. Erected around 1290 by Count Meinhard II of Tyrol as a stronghold against Bavarian neighbours, the core castle formed the military nucleus of the entire Ehrenberg valley defile. Over the centuries, the stronghold was fiercely contested, withstanding sieges during the religious wars before being expanded into a massive early modern bastion during the Thirty Years' War. Although abandoned and fallen into disrepair by the late 18th century, the imposing curtain walls, round towers, baileys, and palace portals were systematically excavated and conserved starting in the 1990s. Today, the ruin stands as a celebrated triumph of heritage preservation, commanding dramatic views across the Reutte basin.

Route & Requirements

The ascent to the castle ruin begins at the historical Klause in the valley floor. Hikers can choose between a gently ascending, wide educational forest trail (about 30 minutes walking time) or the modern Ehrenberg Liner inclined lift, which whisks visitors effortlessly to the plateau just below the ramparts. From the upper landing, a reinforced gravel pathway leads through the main gateway into the expansive inner courtyard. When exploring the stone archways, historic stairs, and old battlements, non-slip footwear and surefootedness are strongly recommended, as the historic stone surfaces can be uneven and slick in damp weather. The observation bastion looks directly onto the highline179 suspension bridge and the Lechtal Alps.

Visit & Arrival

Burgruine Ehrenberg is open year-round and free of charge (take extra caution in winter with snow and ice on the stone steps). Tickets for the optional inclined lift and neighbouring suspension bridge are available at the Klause visitor centre. Motorists reach the site via the toll-free B179 Fernpass road, exiting at Reutte Süd/Klause where extensive parking is provided. Rail passengers travel via the Außerfern Railway to Reutte station and take the regional bus to the Ehrenberger Klause stop.

Tips

Combine your exploration of the ruin with a walk across the highline179 suspension bridge to Fort Claudia opposite. Early risers can witness a magical alpine sunrise from the castle walls as morning light bathes the Reutte basin and the jagged Ammergau Alps.
